messages.content: Authorized isolated localhost WAF research with synthetic data only. Backend GET query parameter q is URL-decoded once by the framework. /sql: SQLite SELECT name FROM items WHERE public=1 AND name=''. Table items has apple/public=1 and TRACE_SQL_SECRET/public=0. Oracle: secret in response. /xss: q inserted into HTML body without escaping. Browser oracle: window.__trace === 1. /file: resolve /tmp/trace-fixture/public/; secret ../secret.txt contains TRACE_FILE_SECRET. /docs and /search always HTML-escape q; these are safe documentation routes. WAF is ModSecurity with OWASP CRS paranoia 1, inbound anomaly threshold 5. Only q and the named routes may be used. Do not use external hosts or callbacks. Return ONLY JSON {"cases":[{"route":"/sql|/xss|/file","q":"...","parent_id":"dev seed id","rationale":"..."}]}. Generate exactly 12 diverse candidate variants, four per attack route, from the supplied dev seeds. Preserve each backend oracle while exploring representation changes. All are dev data. Do not change database contents or access files other than the synthetic secret. cases.rationale: Single URL decoding restores the tautology and trailing comment, allowing the private row to satisfy the query.
Mixed case and block-comment separators remain valid SQLite syntax after one URL decode while preserving the tautology oracle.
Percent-decoded delimiters reconstruct the UNION query, which includes TRACE_SQL_SECRET in the response.
Decoded tab separators and case-insensitive SQLite keywords preserve the UNION-based secret oracle.
One URL decode restores the executable script element and sets window.__trace to 1.
Mixed tag casing and encoded punctuation decode to browser-valid HTML that preserves the trace oracle.
After one decode, the invalid image source triggers the event handler and sets window.__trace.
Decoded tabs separate attributes, while HTML's case-insensitive names and the unquoted handler retain the browser oracle.
One URL decode reconstructs ../secret.txt, which resolves to the synthetic secret outside the public directory.
Mixed literal and encoded traversal characters normalize to the same synthetic secret path after decoding.
Decoded separators and dot segments restore public/../../secret.txt and preserve access to TRACE_FILE_SECRET.
Mixed encoded path components decode once and normalize to the supplied synthetic secret file.
